claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To do this, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you inquiring about for Child Benefit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm inquiring about my one child, Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Let me start by gathering some details about Alex to assess your eligibility.

**What is Alex's date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 6 years old. He was born in 2018.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I need to understand your living situation with Alex.

**Does Alex live with you permanently, or does he live with someone else (such as another parent, grandparent, or in care)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me - he lives with his mum.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that. Let me check the specific rules about this situation to make sure I give you accurate information.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Based on what you've told me, I have an important question:

**Are you making any financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep (such as for clothes, food, housing, or pocket money)? If so, are these contributions at least equal to the amount of Child Benefit you would receive?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not currently contributing financially towards Alex's upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that. Let me also check the main eligibility criteria to ensure I have the complete picture.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I have gathered the information I need to make a determination. Based on the rules I've reviewed:

According to the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you can normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and you live in the UK. You are considered responsible for a child if either you live with them, or you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards looking after them.

In your case:
- Alex is 6 years old and under 16 ✓
- However, Alex lives with his mum, not with you
- You are not making any financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep

The rules state that you'll usually get Child Benefit for 8 weeks after your child goes to live with someone else if nobody else claims. After that 8-week period, you can only continue to receive payments if you contribute to Alex's upkeep by at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment.

Since you are not currently making any financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep, you would not be eligible for Child Benefit beyond the initial 8-week period.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Summary:** Unfortunately, you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex at this time. While Alex meets the age requirement (under 16), Child Benefit requires that you are "responsible" for the child. This means either living with them or making financial contributions towards their upkeep equal to or greater than the Child Benefit payment amount. Since Alex lives with his mother and you're not currently contributing financially towards his care, you don't meet the eligibility criteria.

If circumstances change in the future—for example, if you begin contributing financially towards Alex's upkeep—you would need to contact the Child Benefit Office to discuss your eligibility.
